objectives: Security controls specific to multiple agents

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The security surface increases when agents communicate across multiple runtimes, tools and organizational boundaries.

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments. The security surface increases when agents communicate across multiple runtimes, tools and organizational boundaries.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

sections.title: 22.1 Trust model
sections.body: The parent agent must not automatically trust every assertion or action proposal generated by a child.

sections.title: 22.2 Effective delegation permissions
sections.body:
A simplified least-privilege model is:

\[
P_{effective}\subseteq
P_{principal}\cap
P_{parent}\cap
P_{child}\cap
P_{task}
\]

Actual enterprise systems may permit explicitly governed service delegation, but a child agent must never silently gain greater authority simply because its parent requests it.

sections.title: 22.3 Security controls specific to multiple agents
sections.body:
| Risk | Required control |
|--------|--------|
| Inter-agent prompt injection | Treat received content as untrusted evidence |
| Agent impersonation | Authenticated workload identity |
| Delegation escalation | Explicit scoped authorization |
| Shared memory leakage | Tenant and role-scoped data access |
| Tool privilege escalation | Independent capability gateway |
| Remote data exfiltration | Destination-aware data policy |
| Confused deputy | Enforce requesting principal and purpose |
| Malicious specialist result | Provenance and independent verification |
| Unauthorized artifact retrieval | Object-level authorization |
| Unbounded code execution | Isolated sandbox and resource limits |

sections.title: 22.4 Agent governance registry
sections.body:
Each agent should have a registered business owner, technical owner, deployment version, model configuration, permitted capabilities, risk classification and allowed delegation targets.

A production emergency stop must disable capabilities at protected execution boundaries, not just send a message instructing agents to stop.
